title: Federal Realty Announces Major Overhaul of Huntington Shopping Center in Long Island
summary: Federal Realty Investment Trust is undertaking a $75 million redevelopment of the Huntington Shopping Center in Dix Hills, Long Island. The overhaul includes building a new Whole Foods Market, enhancing parking, installing public seating, and adding new entrances. Construction is expected to finish by the end of 2024, with other tenants remaining open during the process.

title: File your taxes on time with H&R Block Deluxe and State for $33
summary: Amazon is offering H&R Block Tax Software Deluxe + State 2022 for $32.89, a significant discount from its $45 MSRP. This digital download assists with federal and state income tax filing, covers various income streams and deductions, and includes five free federal e-files. While state e-filing costs extra and is not available in New Hampshire, it remains a valuable tool for timely tax preparation.

title: At Snap Inc., Making Augmented Reality Work for Fashion
summary: Snap Inc. is making significant strides in augmented reality (AR) for the fashion industry, with over 200 million Snapchat users engaging with AR daily. Peter Sellis, VP of Product at Snap Inc., discusses how AR technologies, including virtual try-ons and spatial technology, are evolving to enhance shopping experiences, reduce returns, and increase conversions for brands like Prada, Farfetch, and Gucci. The commercial benefits and future product innovations, such as cloth simulation and 3D asset management, are highlighted as key drivers for investment in AR within fashion.

title: Seven Must-Visit Food Halls to Inspire a Gastronomic Getaway
summary: This article highlights seven must-visit food halls across the globe, from Birmingham, Alabama to Tijuana, Mexico, offering diverse culinary experiences for travelers. It emphasizes the growing popularity of food halls as a way to savor local and international cuisine in a relaxed setting, appealing to 51% of global travelers seeking food and drink experiences on their vacations. Each location includes recommendations for local delicacies, additional activities, and nearby hotel stays to inspire gastronomic getaways.

title: Check Point releases 2022 Cloud Security Report
summary: Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. has released its 2022 Cloud Security Report, highlighting the challenges organizations face in securing cloud infrastructures amidst increasing cloud adoption, a cyber-skills shortage, and a rise in cloud security incidents, primarily due to misconfigurations. The report suggests a growing preference for independent cloud security solutions over cloud vendor security to streamline management across multi-cloud environments. TJ Gonen, VP of Cloud Security at Check Point, emphasizes the need for integrated third-party solutions with unified dashboards to simplify cloud security, reduce misconfiguration risks, and support application development in the cloud.

title: Colgate launches $10 ‘premium’ toothpaste
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has launched a new "premium" teeth-whitening toothpaste, Optic White Pro Series, retailing for $10 a tube. This move is part of the company's strategy to raise prices on its products. The launch comes amidst rising inflation, which is squeezing American consumers' finances.

title: 7 E-Commerce Stocks to Buy as Shopify Suffers
summary: Despite a volatile market and a significant drop in high-growth e-commerce stocks like Shopify, the e-commerce industry is projected for substantial growth, with global revenue expected to exceed $7 trillion by 2025. This article identifies seven e-commerce stocks, including Amazon, Etsy, and Target, that offer attractive long-term potential for investors in 2022. Each stock analysis provides financial highlights, market performance, and future outlook, emphasizing their resilience and growth drivers amidst current market headwinds.

title: Amazon Closing All Bookstores, Shops to Focus on Grocery Sector
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is closing all of its physical bookstores, Amazon 4-Star locations, and mall pop-up kiosks to concentrate its brick-and-mortar efforts on the grocery sector. The company will focus on its Amazon Fresh, Whole Foods Market, Amazon Go, and Amazon Style stores, as well as its Just Walk Out technology. This strategic shift involves the closure of 24 bookstores, 33 Amazon 4-Stars, and nine pop-up kiosks, while Whole Foods Market remains its largest physical presence.

title: Amazon Closing Bookstores and Shops to Focus on Grocery Sector
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is closing all of its physical bookstores, "Amazon 4-Star" locations, and mall pop-up kiosks to concentrate its brick-and-mortar retail efforts on the grocery sector. The company plans to prioritize Amazon Fresh, Whole Foods Market, Amazon Go, and Amazon Style stores, along with its "Just Walk Out" technology. Amazon stated it remains committed to physical retail experiences and will assist affected employees in finding new roles within the company.

title: Colgate launches $10 ‘premium’ toothpaste
summary: Colgate-Palmolive is launching a new "premium" Optic White Pro Series toothpaste that costs $10 for a 3-ounce tube, featuring 5% hydrogen peroxide to whiten teeth and remove 15 years of stains. This move comes as the company seeks to raise prices amidst rising inflation, following similar price hikes by other major companies like Amazon and Dollar Tree. The introduction of this high-priced product highlights a trend towards premiumization in consumer goods during a period when many Americans are facing financial strain due to inflation.

title: Amazon to close Green Hills store amid nationwide move
summary: Amazon announced it would close 68 physical retail locations, including its Green Hills Amazon Books store in Nashville, as it shifts its focus toward groceries and fashion. Despite the closures, the company stated it is not abandoning brick-and-mortar sales entirely. This move comes as Amazon opened its first Nashville Amazon Books location in The Mall at Green Hills.

title: DigitalOcean vs Cloudflare — which stock can take advantage of cloud expansion?
summary: This article compares DigitalOcean Holdings (DOCN) and Cloudflare (NET), two cloud computing companies, to determine which is the better investment. DigitalOcean serves developers and SMBs, while Cloudflare focuses on web security and content delivery. The analysis concludes that Cloudflare is the less risky and better investment due to its continued large client growth and potential for SMB expansion, despite DigitalOcean's strong performance and hold in the SMB market.

title: Wide Moat Stock Outlook Remains Compelling
summary: The article discusses the compelling outlook for wide moat stocks, highlighting their historical outperformance, especially in rising interest rate and high inflation environments. It notes that while the VanEck Vectors Morningstar Wide Moat ETF (MOAT) is outperforming the S&P 500 year-to-date, its performance is impacted by highly valued mega-cap growth stocks, which now present opportunities to buy quality at a discount. The analysis emphasizes that wide economic moats protect companies for extended periods, contributing to long-term outperformance with less volatility.

title: Grupo México de Larrea y Telesites de Slim impulsan cierre ganador de la BMV
summary: The Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) closed with gains, driven by companies like Grupo México and Telesites, as oil prices receded. In contrast, Wall Street indices ended lower, and oil prices also fell due to investor concerns about inflation, Federal Reserve policy, and the impact of the Russia-Ukraine conflict on commodity markets. The article also details the performance of various companies on both the BMV and Wall Street, as well as the impact on global markets and bond yields.

title: How A Failed Experiment Led To Bubble Wrap
summary: Bubble Wrap, a ubiquitous packaging material, was created accidentally in 1957 by Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes. Their initial attempt to create textured wallpaper resulted in air bubbles trapped between plastic sheets. After failing to market it as insulation, they founded Sealed Air Corp. in 1960, and their product found its true purpose protecting delicate equipment for IBM, leading to its widespread adoption and the company's success.

title: How Hyperscale Data Centers are reshaping India’s IT
summary: Hyperscale data centers are critical infrastructure for companies like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, providing dedicated computing resources to handle massive user demands. These facilities are essential for the digital economy, supporting everything from emails to online shopping, and their importance has grown with trends like remote work and emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. India is poised for significant growth in its data center industry, driven by government incentives and an increasing need for robust data storage and processing capabilities, despite environmental concerns related to energy consumption.

title: Sonos Roam SL vs Sonos Roam: which Bluetooth speaker will be the best?
summary: This article compares the Sonos Roam SL and the Sonos Roam, two portable Bluetooth speakers from Sonos, to help consumers decide which one best suits their needs. The key difference lies in the Roam having a built-in microphone for voice controls, Auto Trueplay, and Sound Swap, features absent from the more affordable Roam SL. Both speakers share the same design, battery life, and core audio technology, making the choice dependent on budget and the importance of smart features.

title: Cloud management provider Cloocus receives $41 mn in Series B funding
summary: Cloud management service provider Cloocus Co. has secured $40.8 million (50 billion won) in Series B funding from SK Inc. C&C as part of a larger 100 billion won round. This investment follows significant funding rounds for other Korean cloud MSPs like Megazone Cloud and Bespin Global. The capital injections reflect a turnaround for Korean MSPs, driven by increased demand for cloud services due to the pandemic and the growing adoption of SaaS and multicloud strategies.

title: Your Fenty Beauty Favorites Are Now Available At Ulta Beauty
summary: Rihanna's Fenty Beauty line is expanding its retail presence by launching in over 1,300 Ulta Beauty locations, both online and in-store, starting March 6th. This move aims to make the popular beauty brand more accessible to a wider audience, fulfilling Rihanna's vision of global inclusion. Fans can expect a sneak peek of available products on February 28th before the official launch.

title: Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Stock Price Has Fallen 12.8% in 2022. Should You Buy It?
summary: Alphabet's stock (GOOGL) has dropped 12.8% in 2022, leading many to question if it's a good buying opportunity. Despite plateauing ad revenues, Google is expanding into cloud services and cybersecurity, highlighted by its acquisition of Mandiant. The company is considered attractive at current prices, though antitrust concerns remain a risk.

title: Rivian is sued by shareholder after rolling back electric vehicle price hikes
summary: A shareholder has filed a lawsuit against Rivian Automotive Inc, alleging the company misled investors during its IPO by underpricing its electric vehicles. This alleged mispricing led to swift, unpopular price hikes that were later rolled back. The lawsuit claims these price adjustments tarnished Rivian's reputation and put preorders at risk.

title: Starbucks, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo suspend operations in Russia; Amazon suspends web services sign-ups
summary: Coca-Cola, Starbucks, PepsiCo, and Amazon have announced the suspension of their operations in Russia in response to the country's invasion of Ukraine. Coca-Cola stated it was pausing business, while Starbucks is suspending all business activity and closing stores. Amazon Web Services is no longer allowing new sign-ups in Russia or Belarus, emphasizing it does not have infrastructure there and will suspend services for those promoting violence.

title: Shipping Fraud Increased Nearly 800% Worldwide in the Past Year
summary: TransUnion's 2022 Global Digital Fraud Trends Report reveals that shipping fraud surged by 780.5% globally year-over-year in 2021, and over 1,500% from 2019 to 2021, making it the fastest-growing type of digital fraud worldwide. This increase is primarily attributed to the continuous growth of e-commerce, with fraudsters targeting areas where consumers are most active. The report also highlights significant increases in other fraud types and identifies industries most affected by digital fraud globally and in the United States, such as gaming, travel and leisure, and financial services.

title: Rivian is sued for allegedly misleading investors about electric vehicle prices
summary: Rivian Automotive Inc is facing a class-action lawsuit from a shareholder who claims the company misled investors by initially underpricing its electric vehicles, leading to unpopular price hikes that were later rolled back. The lawsuit alleges Rivian concealed that its R1S SUV and R1T pickup trucks were so underpriced they would require rapid price increases after its November IPO, damaging the company's reputation and risking pre-order cancellations. The plaintiff, Charles Larry Crews, cites the swift rollback of price increases and an apology from CEO R.J. Scaringe as "futile attempts at damage control."

title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split, $10 bln share buyback
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has announced a 20-for-1 stock split and authorized a $10 billion share buyback plan, causing its shares to rise by 7% in extended trading. This marks Amazon's first stock split since 1999, aimed at making shares more accessible to investors and increasing flexibility for employees managing equity. Trading with the new share price will commence on June 6.

title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split, $10 billion buyback
summary: Amazon announced its first stock split since 1999, proposing a 20-for-1 split that sent its stock soaring by 6% in extended trading. The company's board also authorized a share buyback program of up to $10 billion. This move follows similar stock splits by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Apple, and Tesla, aiming to make shares more accessible to investors and benefit employees.

title: Lumen (like the field) is pulling out of Russia. What's next?
summary: Lumen, an internet backbone company known for its naming rights to a Seattle sports stadium, is pulling its services out of Russia. This decision, following similar moves by other companies like Cogen, could significantly impact Russia's internet access, potentially leading to slower connectivity and isolation from the global web. An editor from DatacenterDynamics explains that Lumen's role as a major international transit provider means its withdrawal is a substantial move towards disconnecting Russia.

title: Sezzle Answers Call of the Wild by Bringing Buy Now, Pay Later to Sportsman's Guide
summary: Sezzle has partnered with Sportsman's Guide to offer flexible "buy now, pay later" payment options to its online customers. This partnership introduces a new biweekly interest-free installment plan and powers Sportsman's Guide's existing "4-Pay Monthly" product for Club Members, aiming to provide increased buying power and responsible budgeting for outdoor enthusiasts. The collaboration also helps Sportsman's Guide attract Sezzle's Millennial and Gen Z demographics, while Sezzle users benefit from the potential to build credit through Sezzle Up.

title: UNFI gets Q2 boost from independents, Whole Foods
summary: United Natural Foods Inc. (UNFI) reported record net sales of $7.42 billion for its fiscal second quarter, largely driven by strong performances in its Independent and Supernatural (Whole Foods Market) segments. The company's "Fuel the Future" strategy, focusing on customer service, own brands, and fresh categories, is credited for the growth. UNFI also updated its fiscal 2022 guidance, slightly raising its net sales forecast.

title: Walmart to offer its Walmart Plus service to its workers for free
summary: Walmart announced it will provide its Walmart Plus membership service for free to all part-time and full-time employees in the United States. This move comes as retailers compete for workers in a tight labor market, with Walmart joining other companies offering increased benefits. The Walmart Plus service, which includes free delivery, fuel discounts, and other perks, is seen as a rival to Amazon Prime and could significantly expand its subscriber base by including Walmart's 1.6 million employees.

title: Amazon to split stock for the first time since the dot-com boom, after gains of more than 4,500%
summary: Amazon announced its first stock split in over 20 years, a 20-to-1 split, after its shares gained more than 4,500% since its last split in 1999. The company also plans to repurchase $10 billion in shares. This move is contingent on a shareholder vote in May, with the split expected around June 3.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Approves 20-for-1 Stock Split, $10B Buyback
summary: Amazon's board of directors approved a 20-for-1 stock split and a $10 billion share buyback. This marks Amazon's first stock split since 1999 and is intended to make shares more accessible to a broader range of investors and employees. Other major tech companies like Apple, Tesla, and Alphabet have also undertaken stock splits recently.

title: CrowdStrike’s Crowd-Pleaser; Build-A-Bear’s Blunder; Asana’s Attitude Adjustment
summary: This article discusses the financial performance and market outlook for several companies. CrowdStrike reported impressive earnings and strong guidance, positioning it well in the growing cybersecurity market. Build-A-Bear Workshop issued a cautious 2022 outlook due to inflation, leading to investor concern, while Amazon announced a 20-for-1 stock split, mirroring Alphabet's earlier move. Additionally, Asana reported significant losses despite revenue growth, and PayPal faced a downgrade from BofA Securities due to concerns about the Russia-Ukraine conflict's impact.

title: Disney ‘Taking Steps to Pause’ All Business in Russia
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced it is "taking steps to pause" all other businesses in Russia, beyond its initial halt on new movie releases, due to the "unprovoked invasion of Ukraine" and escalating humanitarian crisis. This includes content and product licensing, Disney Cruise Line activities, National Geographic magazine and tours, local content productions, and linear channels. Disney stated that while some activities can be paused immediately, others will take time due to contractual complexities, and staff in Russia will remain employed.

title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split
summary: Amazon announced a 20-for-1 stock split, following similar moves by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Apple, and Tesla. The article explains that a stock split divides existing shares into multiple, smaller-priced shares without changing the overall value of an investor's holdings or the company's market capitalization. Stock splits are often done to increase a stock's liquidity and make it more accessible to a wider range of investors, though in an era of fractional shares, some of the practical impact is diminished.

title: Hayward Introduces Advanced AquaRite S3 Salt Sanitization System
summary: Hayward Holdings, Inc. has launched its advanced AquaRite S3 Salt Chlorination System, which offers enhanced pool control and integrates with Hayward’s Omni automation platform for intuitive management. This new system provides an eco-friendly and cost-effective alternative to traditional chlorine sanitization, featuring broad salt concentration compatibility and Hayward TurboCell® technology for easy maintenance. The AquaRite S3 aims to address chlorine shortages and cater to environmentally conscious consumers through pool professionals.

title: Amazon surges as stock split, buyback excite investors
summary: Amazon's stock surged over 5% after the company announced a 20-for-1 stock split and a $10 billion share buyback, aiming to attract more investors and boost confidence. This move follows a period of lackluster performance for the e-commerce giant, despite its substantial growth since its IPO. The stock split, the first since 1999, and the buyback are seen as psychological boosts and a signal that management views the stock as undervalued.

title: eBay expects revenue growth of up to 6% in 2023, launches digital wallet
summary: E-commerce company eBay (EBAY.O) anticipates revenue growth of 5% to 6% in fiscal 2023 and introduced its first digital wallet to allow customers to use sales proceeds for purchases or expenses. The company also launched eBay Vault for trading cards and collectibles, despite facing stiff competition from rivals like Amazon and waning online demand. eBay forecasts higher revenue and adjusted profit growth for fiscal 2024.

title: Goodyear debuts 'last-mile' delivery truck tires
summary: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. has introduced two new lines of fuel-efficient truck tires, the Fuel Max RSA ULT and Endurance RSA ULT, specifically designed for the growing last-mile delivery sector. These tires cater to both electric and internal combustion engine vehicles, with the Endurance RSA ULT being notably "Electric Drive Ready" and designed for higher load capacities. Both lines feature advanced technologies aimed at improving tread life, durability, traction, and fuel efficiency for urban delivery applications.

title: The Climate Pledge announces nearly 100 new signatories
summary: The Climate Pledge, co-founded by Amazon and Global Optimism, has announced nearly 100 new signatories, bringing the total to over 300 companies committed to reaching net-zero carbon by 2040. These companies, spanning 51 industries and 29 countries, pledge to regularly measure and report greenhouse gas emissions, implement decarbonization strategies, and neutralize remaining emissions. Notable new signatories include Maersk, SAP, Weyerhaeuser, Sunrun, and HARMAN, all actively pursuing significant carbon reduction initiatives.

title: The Importance of Ink Cartridge Recycling
summary: This article discusses the environmental benefits of recycling ink cartridges, highlighting HP's closed-loop recycling program, Planet Partners. It explains how recycling helps reduce plastic waste, supports communities, and ensures the use of quality OEM products. The article also provides multiple convenient methods for consumers to recycle their used HP ink cartridges.

title: IonQ to Present Research at American Physical Society (APS) Annual Meeting 2022
summary: IonQ announced its participation in the American Physical Society (APS) March Meeting 2022, where co-founder and CTO Jungsang Kim will be honored for his pioneering contributions to quantum computing. IonQ researchers will present new advances in quantum chemistry simulations, risk aggregation using quantum generative modeling, and general quantum learning of joint probability distribution functions. The company will also discuss application-oriented performance benchmarks for quantum computing, including its new #AQ single-number benchmark.

title: eBay Ventures Offers Venture Capital To Innovative Founders
summary: eBay Ventures, the venture capital arm of eBay Inc., offers funding and strategic expertise to innovative founders in areas adjacent to eBay's core business. The firm has made its first investment in Norwegian second-hand marketplace Tise, backing it in a $20 million funding round. eBay Ventures aims to support startups that can bring new value, expand business, and provide a competitive advantage, reflecting eBay's "build, buy, or partner" strategy.

title: Four ways companies can find the ‘hidden talent’
summary: Many companies struggle to find talent despite a large pool of "hidden workers." This article outlines four strategies for companies to tap into this underserved talent pool. These strategies include implementing "returnships," upskilling current employees, directly collaborating with educational institutions, and removing college degree requirements from job descriptions.

title: The 7 Best Wi-Fi Routers for Long Range and Reliability
summary: This article reviews the seven best Wi-Fi routers for extended range and reliable performance, aimed at improving home network coverage and speed. It covers various router types, including mesh systems and gaming routers, highlighting their key features, specifications, pros, and cons. The guide helps users choose a router based on their specific needs, such as coverage area, number of devices, and budget.

title: How to set up and use Alexa voice commands on your Fossil smartwatch
summary: Fossil Gen 6 smartwatch owners can now use Amazon Alexa instead of Google Assistant, with support rolling out in spring 2022 for Fossil, Skagen, and Michael Kors devices. This guide details the setup process, which requires linking the Alexa watch app to the Alexa mobile app on an Android phone, and explains how to use Alexa for various commands like playing music, asking questions, controlling smart home devices, and making calls. Alexa responses are displayed on the watch screen rather than being read aloud, and the functionality works alongside Google Assistant.

title: Best AirPlay speakers in 2022: Apple, Sonos, Bose, and more
summary: This article reviews the best AirPlay-compatible speakers available in 2022, featuring top brands like Apple, Sonos, and Bose. It categorizes speakers by their ideal use cases, such as all-around performance, TV integration, portability, and premium audio, helping users choose the best option for their iPhone, iPad, or Apple TV. Each recommendation includes pricing information and highlights key features like AirPlay 2 support, smart assistant integration, and sound quality.

title: Amazon, Walmart Online Orders Likely Delayed by China Lockdowns
summary: Online orders from platforms like Amazon and Walmart may experience delays due to new COVID-19 lockdowns and restrictions in key manufacturing hubs in China, including Shenzhen and Dongguan. The shutdowns are causing significant disruption to production and delivery of goods, impacting exporters and logistics operations, and further complicating an already challenging period for Chinese sellers on global platforms.

title: Fossil Group confirms Alexa app rollout on Gen 6 smartwatches, more features to come
summary: Fossil Group has confirmed the rollout of the Amazon Alexa app to its Gen 6 smartwatches, including models from Fossil and Skagen. Users can now access Alexa via a tile or button shortcut for tasks like playing music, checking weather, and controlling smart home devices. While lacking always-listening functionality, Fossil plans to expand the features of both the Alexa tile and app on these newer Wear OS smartwatches.

title: Goodyear Launches New Last-Mile Delivery Tires
summary: Goodyear has introduced two new tire lines, the Endurance RSA ULT and Fuel Max RSA ULT, designed for the growing last-mile delivery sector. The Endurance RSA ULT is engineered for higher load capacities of electric commercial vehicles, making it Goodyear's first "electric drive ready" tire, while the Fuel Max RSA ULT focuses on balancing traction, fuel efficiency, and mileage for regional pickup and delivery. These new tires aim to meet the demands of e-commerce growth and fleet goals for cost savings and sustainability.

title: e-commerce logistics market grew by 19.9% in 2021 | Ti-insight
summary: The global e-commerce logistics market experienced significant growth of 19.9% in 2021, reaching a value of €441.47bn, despite a slowdown from its 2020 peak. The market is projected to grow at an 11.8% CAGR from 2021-2026, with cross-border e-commerce growing at 10.65%. While Asia Pacific currently leads, North America is forecasted to become the largest e-commerce logistics market by 2026.

title: Goldman Sachs ActiveBeta World Low Vol Plus Equity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:GLOV)
summary: This article provides details on the Goldman Sachs ActiveBeta World Low Vol Plus Equity ETF (GLOV), including its stock price, key statistics, and holdings. GLOV invests in large- and mid-cap stocks in developed markets, focusing on value, momentum, quality, and low volatility factors. The ETF was launched on March 15, 2022, and is managed by Goldman Sachs.

title: Walmart wants to hire more than 50,000 workers in new business push
summary: Walmart plans to hire over 50,000 new employees by the end of April to support its expansion into new business areas like online grocery, advertising, and its third-party marketplace. The new roles will include personal shoppers, delivery drivers, and data scientists. This hiring push comes in a tight labor market where Walmart will compete with other retailers for workers.

title: Morgan Health joins $23M series B round for Embold Health
summary: Morgan Health, JPMorgan Chase's healthcare arm, invested $5 million in Embold Health's $23 million Series B funding round. Embold Health is a physician-led data analytics company focused on improving healthcare quality and cost. This investment aligns with Morgan Health's mission to enhance employer healthcare by partnering with innovative organizations and making strategic investments in promising health solutions.

title: Instacart Unveils Shoppable Recipes, New Product Integrations With TikTok, Tasty, Hearst Magazines And More
summary: Instacart has launched "Shoppable Recipes," a new feature that allows users to seamlessly purchase ingredients for recipes found on platforms like TikTok and Hearst Magazines' food properties (e.g., Delish). This initiative aims to transform online recipe browsing into immediate action, providing a new avenue for food creators to monetize content and for Instacart's retail partners to reach new customers. The integration leverages Instacart's extensive grocery catalog and AI to enable quick delivery of in-stock items.

title: Tradesy online fashion marketplace acquired
summary: The online fashion marketplace Tradesy has been acquired, a move that highlights a shared ambition to accelerate the growth of the circular fashion economy. This acquisition comes as the global market value for secondhand and resale apparel was estimated at $36 billion in 2021.

title: Top 10 Sites Like QVC [ Best Alternatives To Website Like QVC ]
summary: This article lists the top 10 alternative websites to QVC, highlighting those offering easy payment plans and similar product categories like home furnishings, electronics, beauty, and apparel. It details features of each site, such as payment options, product variety, and user experience, catering to online shoppers looking for flexible purchasing choices.

title: Electronic Arts Launches MLB Tap Sports™ Baseball 2022
summary: Electronic Arts (NASDAQ: EA) has released MLB Tap Sports Baseball 2022, the latest installment of its free-to-play mobile baseball franchise, featuring Philadelphia Phillies right fielder Bryce Harper as the cover athlete. This release marks the first game from Electronic Arts following its acquisition of Glu Mobile and introduces new features like Champions Tier, Avatar Gear, improved visuals, and a revamped UI. The game is available as a free download worldwide on the App Store, Google Play, and Amazon Appstore, building on the franchise's over 56 million global downloads.

title: Musk’s Starlink Brings Internet to Ukraine, and Attention to a New Space Race
summary: Elon Musk's Starlink has provided crucial satellite broadband service to Ukraine, particularly as Russian forces target infrastructure. This assistance highlights the growing importance of low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, championed by companies like SpaceX and Amazon, in a new space race for global internet connectivity. These LEO satellites offer a smaller, more affordable alternative to traditional geostationary satellites for delivering internet access.

title: Amazon closes $8.5bn deal to buy MGM movie studio
authors: ['David McLaughlin and Matt Day and Bloomberg']
summary: Amazon has completed its $8.5 billion acquisition of Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) after regulators did not challenge the deal, making it Amazon's largest acquisition since Whole Foods in 2017. MGM's extensive catalog, including the James Bond franchise and 25,000 hours of content, will bolster Amazon's Prime Video and IMDb TV streaming offerings. Despite concerns from some antitrust critics, experts believe a legal challenge against the deal would likely fail as it doesn't significantly alter market competition.

title: Why banks and NATO are worrying about a future ‘Quantum attack’
summary: The article discusses the growing concern among banks and organizations like NATO about the potential for "quantum attacks" as quantum computing technology advances. Andersen Cheng, CEO of Post Quantum, warns that powerful quantum computers capable of cracking current encryption methods may be closer than initially thought, posing a significant threat to critical communications, financial data, and cryptocurrencies. The piece highlights how various nations are investing heavily in quantum technology and the commercial sector is beginning to prepare for this shift.

title: After nearly 2 decades of decline, what’s next for office supplies stores?
summary: The office supplies store sector has been in consistent decline for nearly two decades, largely due to competition from e-commerce and generalist retailers, and the digitization of work. Despite a boom in home office setups during the pandemic, specialized retailers like Staples and Office Depot have not seen a proportional increase in sales, as consumers increasingly turn to online channels and mass merchants. The future of the sector might involve further consolidation, with Staples' recurring bids for ODP (Office Depot's parent company) potentially leading to a single dominant player in a shrinking market.

title: Berkshire Hathaway shares topped $500,000 each—here's why Warren Buffett says he'll never split the stock
summary: Class A shares of Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway recently closed above $500,000 each for the first time, making it the sixth most valuable company in the U.S. Despite calls for a stock split to lower share prices, Buffett has consistently refused, arguing that the high price attracts sophisticated, long-term investors. He believes a split would lead to a less aligned shareholder base and offers no intrinsic value if not tied to company growth.

title: Starbucks plans to phase out its single-use coffee cups
summary: Starbucks is aiming to phase out its single-use coffee cups as part of a larger goal to cut its overall waste in half by 2030. The company is exploring cup-sharing programs as a primary method to achieve this environmental objective.

title: Target embraces solar panels, with California store its first 'net zero' building
summary: Target Corp. has announced its first "net zero" store in Vista, California, designed to produce more energy than it consumes. The refurbished store features thousands of solar panels and a carbon dioxide refrigeration system, serving as a model for future sustainability efforts. This initiative is part of Target's broader goal to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040 and source all its electricity from renewable sources by 2030.

title: The Impact of Design on the Employee Experience
summary: Workday's Chief Design Officer, Jeff Gelfuso, emphasizes the importance of delivering seamless and engaging end-to-end experiences for employees within enterprise software, mirroring consumer software expectations. He discusses how Workday is achieving this through simplification, personalization, connectedness, and data-driven insights. The article highlights key design principles and Workday's initiatives like Engage, Everywhere, and Empower to improve the employee experience.

title: Amazon.com closes deal to buy MGM movie studio
summary: Amazon.com Inc has finalized its $8.5 billion acquisition of MGM, integrating the renowned movie studio known for "Rocky" and James Bond into its ecosystem. This move aims to enhance Amazon's Prime streaming service by adding over 4,000 film titles and numerous television shows to better compete with rivals like Netflix and Disney+. The deal closed after clearing regulatory hurdles in both the U.S. and Europe, with Amazon welcoming all MGM employees and leadership.

title: Jury: Employer’s DEI training didn’t conflict with worker’s religious beliefs
summary: A federal jury ruled that a born-again Christian employee's religious beliefs did not conflict with his employer's mandatory Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) training. The employee, who was later fired, had refused to complete a course question about identifying harassment of a transgender co-worker, claiming a conflict with his beliefs. The jury found that while he had sincerely held beliefs, they did not conflict with the company's employment requirement, highlighting the employer's appropriate response of focusing on workplace behavior rather than personal beliefs.

title: Amazon to open new Prince George’s delivery station — built for it from the ground up
summary: Amazon plans to open a new 130,000-square-foot delivery station in Prince George's County, Maryland, in 2023. This facility will be the e-commerce giant's first delivery station in Greater Washington to be built for it from the ground up. The development signals Amazon's continued expansion of its logistics network in the region.

title: Kroger: Redefining grocery customers experience
summary: Kroger is continuously innovating to enhance the grocery customer experience, from its founding as the nation's first supermarket to its current efforts led by Kroger Labs. The company focuses on rapid, incremental innovations based on customer feedback, leveraging collaborations with partners like Instacart, Bed Bath & Beyond, and Deloitte. Through technology, university partnerships, and a commitment to diverse thinking, Kroger aims to create seamless in-store and digital shopping experiences, driven by high-impact R&D and a culture that empowers associates.

title: Is Sonos looking to jump into the streaming video market?
summary: Sonos, known for its connected audio devices, might be expanding into the streaming video market based on recent job postings. These postings refer to a "Next Generation Home Theater OS" and seek candidates with experience in streaming media, suggesting the company could be developing a video streaming device or a soundbar with integrated smart-TV app capabilities. This move would mark a significant step beyond its current audio-focused product line.

title: The BlackBerry veteran who took on Google and won
summary: Patrick Spence, CEO of Sonos, a veteran of BlackBerry (formerly Research In Motion), successfully led Sonos in a patent infringement lawsuit against Google. The U.S. International Trade Commission ruled in favor of Sonos, affirming that Google infringed on five of Sonos's patents related to smart speaker technology. This victory demonstrates that smaller companies can win intellectual property disputes against large tech giants, emboldening Sonos and potentially setting the stage for future actions against other major players like Amazon.

title: Amazon union backers see bright future for organizing despite tough odds
summary: Amazon workers in Bessemer, Alabama, are in the midst of a new unionization vote, buoyed by a resurgent labor movement despite facing long odds. The previous union election was overturned due to Amazon's interference, and despite a two-to-one margin of victory for Amazon last time, organizers are hopeful a strong showing will encourage further union efforts across Amazon and other companies like Starbucks. Concerns over productivity targets and working conditions, coupled with increased public and governmental approval for unions, are fueling this renewed push for organized labor.

title: Sources: Amazon snaps up more industrial space in Gaston County
summary: Amazon has reportedly leased a 286,275-square-foot facility at the Gateway85 industrial park in Gaston County, further expanding its regional industrial footprint. While the park's leasing agent confirmed the lease, the tenant's identity was not disclosed. This move highlights Amazon's rapid growth in the Charlotte industrial market.

title: This World Water Day, We Celebrate a Milestone for Enriching Communities Along Our Supply Chains
summary: Gap Inc. is celebrating a significant milestone on World Water Day, having empowered 1.5 million people in India to improve their access to water and sanitation through the USAID Gap Inc. Women + Water Alliance. This initiative is part of Gap Inc.'s broader commitment to water stewardship and aims to reach 2 million people by 2023, while also supporting women's empowerment in water-stressed communities where cotton, a high-water-use crop, is grown for their supply chain. The program involves various partners like CARE, WaterAid, Water.org, and ISC, working on different aspects from women's self-efficacy to sustainable farming practices.

title: MyTheresa Quietly Launched on JD.com, Readies for Marathon in China
summary: Luxury e-commerce site MyTheresa has quietly launched on JD.com in China, listing over 2,200 items from 49 brands as part of a cautious "marathon, not a sprint" entry into the challenging market. The company aims to test the waters with this soft launch before making any official announcements, as evidenced by only one sale so far, while also leveraging China's increased brand interest in JD.com following Alibaba's antitrust scrutiny. MyTheresa is distinguishing itself by offering European dispatch and a 30-day free return policy, with pricing on JD.com reportedly slightly lower than local Chinese rates due to included duties and import fees.

title: Nvidia debuts next-generation H100 GPUs, its most powerful chips yet
summary: Nvidia has unveiled its next-generation H100 GPUs, built on the new Hopper architecture, which promise an order of magnitude performance improvement over previous models. These chips feature 80 billion transistors, a Transformer Engine for accelerating AI language models, and HBM3 memory. The H100 GPUs are designed for advanced AI workloads, including real-time inference, and will be available to customers and cloud providers in the third quarter.

title: NVIDIA Announces Availability of Jetson AGX Orin Developer Kit to Advance Robotics and Edge AI
summary: NVIDIA has announced the availability of its Jetson AGX Orin developer kit, a powerful AI supercomputer designed for advanced robotics, autonomous machines, and edge computing. This new kit offers over eight times the processing power of its predecessor, the Jetson AGX Xavier, while maintaining a compact form factor. NVIDIA expects the Jetson AGX Orin to accelerate the development of next-generation robotics and edge AI products across various industries, supported by a broad ecosystem of partners and customers.

title: StarTree brings Apache Pinot real-time database to the cloud
summary: StarTree has launched its cloud service for the Apache Pinot real-time OLAP database, making it easier for organizations to deploy and manage this technology. This service, initially offered with a "bring your own cloud" (BYOC) model, allows users to run Pinot in their private cloud while StarTree handles management. Apache Pinot, originally from LinkedIn, is designed for rapid querying of large datasets for analytics and operational dashboards, and StarTree's offering aims to simplify data ingestion and observability.

title: After nearly a decade in the red, Destination XL posts record profit and sales
summary: Destination XL reported record sales and profits for fiscal 2021, achieving its first positive annual profit since 2012 with net income of $56.7 million and sales exceeding half a billion dollars for the first time. The company also eliminated its long-term debt and revolver, a significant turnaround after nearly a decade of losses and pandemic-induced challenges. This success is attributed to cost-cutting, lease negotiations, and a "transformative digital strategy" focused on consumer research and fit expertise.

title: Booz Allen makes investment in Wisconsin AI company
summary: Booz Allen Hamilton has invested in Synthetaic, a Wisconsin-based artificial intelligence company. This move by the McLean IT consulting giant could signal a future acquisition target, according to the article. The investment was reported by the Washington Business Journal.

title: Nvidia CEO says interested in exploring chip manufacturing with Intel
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed interest in exploring Intel's chip manufacturing services. Intel, which aims to expand its foundry business, confirmed ongoing discussions with Nvidia. This potential collaboration could be significant for Intel's efforts to attract external chip design companies to its factories.

title: Amazon continues to expand presence here
summary: Amazon is significantly expanding its presence in the Spokane area with two major construction projects valued at $56 million. These include a large sorting facility on the West Plains and a last-mile delivery facility in Airway Heights. The new facilities will add hundreds of jobs and are part of Amazon's ongoing development in the region, following the opening of an Air Cargo facility and a fulfillment center last year.

title: Etsy Sellers Are Protesting New Fees On The Platform
summary: Thousands of Etsy sellers and customers are protesting a new 30% increase in transaction fees, calling it "pandemic profiteering" and planning a strike and customer boycott. Sellers argue that Etsy's new policies prioritize short-term revenue over the interests of its creators and that previous fee hikes did not lead to promised improvements. This latest increase is seen by many long-time sellers as the "final straw," prompting calls for stronger collective action and even helping sellers transition off the platform.

title: Netflix buys another video game studio as it builds out its gaming business. (Published 2022)
summary: Netflix announced it acquired Boss Fight Entertainment, a mobile game developer, marking its third studio purchase as it expands into the video game market. This move is part of Netflix's strategy to differentiate itself by leveraging popular shows for game development and eventually creating original games, aiming for a careful expansion after seeing other tech companies struggle in the gaming industry.

title: Instacart’s new tech platform lets retailers sell ads on their sites
summary: Instacart has launched Instacart Platform, a new suite of digital services for grocers and retailers that includes fulfillment, insights, and advertising options through Carrot Ads. This platform allows retailers to leverage Instacart's ad tech and data insights to monetize their e-commerce properties, with a revenue-sharing model. The move aims to strengthen relationships with retailers and integrate Instacart further into their operations, particularly for mid-sized and smaller grocery retailers.

title: Amazon Stock Rally Erases Losses for the Year
summary: Amazon.com Inc. shares rallied, becoming the first megacap tech stock to recover its losses for the year,

title: FedEx Corp. founder Fred Smith will step down as CEO in June
summary: Fred Smith, founder of FedEx Corp., announced he will step down as CEO on June 1, transitioning to executive chairman. Raj Subramaniam, current president and chief operating officer, will succeed him as CEO and president. Smith founded FedEx in 1973 and oversaw its growth into a global package-delivery giant, while Subramaniam has been with the company since 1991.

title: Sea e-commerce unit Shopee to shut India operations
summary: Sea Ltd's e-commerce unit, Shopee, is withdrawing from India's retail market just months after launching operations, effective March 29. This follows its exit from France and India's ban on Sea's gaming app "Free Fire." The company cited "global market uncertainties" and a weak growth outlook, with revenue growth for its e-commerce business expected to halve in 2022.

title: CEO interview: Silicon Labs’ Matt Johnson on balancing breadth and focus
summary: Matt Johnson, CEO of Silicon Labs, discusses the company's strategic shift to focus entirely on the IoT market after divesting its infrastructure and automotive businesses. He highlights the importance of offering complete, application- and software-led solutions for diverse wireless technologies in IoT, emphasizing security and continuous integration for cost, performance, and power reduction. Johnson also touches on the company's approach to manufacturing and capital deployment, including M&A and share repurchases.

title: AWS for Games
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has launched "AWS for Games," a new initiative designed to help game developers create and manage gaming experiences by providing purpose-built services, solutions, and partners. This program aligns AWS capabilities across six key areas: Cloud Game Development, Game Servers, Game Security, Live Operations, Game Analytics, and Game AI & ML. The goal is to simplify cloud adoption for game companies, reduce development resources, and accelerate time to market.

title: Consumers Will Increase Gift Card Purchases in 2022, a Fiserv Study Says
summary: A Fiserv Inc. study indicates that consumers will increase gift card purchases in 2022, primarily due to inflation, supply-chain shortages, and their perception of gift cards as an appropriate alternative to tangible gifts. The study highlights interest in both physical and digital gift cards, with birthdays being the most popular occasion for giving, and Visa Inc. and American Express Co. cards being the most popular brands. Promotions are also expected to drive gift card sales.

title: Global Paper and Paperboard Packaging Market is estimated
summary: The Global Paper and Paperboard Packaging Market is projected to reach US$ 298.3 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 3.3% from its 2020 valuation of US$ 215.34 billion. This growth is driven by the increasing demand for eco-friendly packaging solutions and the rise of online shopping. Key market players include DS Smith Plc., Amcor Ltd., and International Paper Company.

title: Doolies' kid snacks help little tummies move
summary: Doolies, a new snack brand from General Mills' corporate venture studio G-Works, offers fruit-forward snacks designed to help alleviate occasional constipation in children. Co-founded by parents, the products combine fiber (psyllium husk) and fruits like prunes and pears, aiming for both efficacy and kid appeal with formats such as Fruit Filled Bars and Cashew Fruit & Nut Bites. The brand addresses a common issue, with 30% of U.S. children experiencing occasional constipation, and focuses on creating intuitive, tasty solutions for digestive health.

title: Palo Alto Networks teams with Amazon to bring next-gen firewall service to AWS
summary: Palo Alto Networks has partnered with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to launch Cloud NGFW for AWS, a next-generation firewall service designed to secure AWS deployments. This managed service shifts operational responsibility to Palo Alto Networks, offering advanced URL filtering, threat prevention, and App-ID for simplified deployment and enhanced security. It integrates with AWS Gateway Load Balancer for high availability and elastic scaling, and with AWS Firewall Manager for consistent policy management.

title: IonQ Named As One Of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies
summary: IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), a leader in trapped-ion quantum computing, has been recognized on TIME’s annual TIME100 Most Influential Companies list for its leadership in commercializing quantum computing. The company was included in the "New Frontiers" category, acknowledging its extraordinary impact and recent achievements, including the introduction of IonQ Aria, the world's most powerful quantum computer. This recognition follows a year of significant business momentum and technical breakthroughs for IonQ.

title: McDonald’s Linked to Amazon Deforestation in New Report
summary: A new report by Repórter Brasil links McDonald’s to deforestation and labor abuses in Brazil's Amazon rainforest and Pantanal wetlands. The report alleges that beef from illegally cleared ranches was channeled through farms to hide its origin before reaching slaughterhouses that supply McDonald's. European unions are using this report to pressure McDonald's into disclosing detailed risks in its supply chain under a French vigilance law.

title: Fruit + Fiber + probiotics: General Mills unveils Doolies snacks for kids
summary: General Mills has launched Doolies, a new line of fruit and fiber-packed snacks formulated with probiotics for young children, aimed at addressing occasional constipation. Developed by General Mills’ G-Works venture studio, Doolies bars and bites contain psyllium husk fiber, inulin, and Kerry’s BC30 probiotic, designed to balance taste appeal and functional benefits for picky eaters. The products are launching on Amazon, with extensive testing conducted to ensure efficacy and palatability for kids.

title: TForce Logistics Expands in Greater Toronto Area, Opens Fourth Distribution Centre in Hamilton
summary: TForce Logistics has expanded its presence in the Greater Toronto Area by opening its fourth distribution center in Hamilton, Ontario. This new 8,140 square foot facility aims to increase capacity for eCommerce volumes and meet the rising demand for expedited final-mile delivery services, providing next-day delivery along the Highway 401 corridor from Hamilton to Niagara Falls. The expansion supports both business-to-business and eCommerce consumer deliveries, enhancing TForce Logistics' integrated network in North America.

title: Why you need a total experience strategy to drive CX and EX
summary: This article discusses the growing importance of a "total experience" strategy, which integrates customer experience (CX), employee experience (EX), user experience (UX), and multiexperience (MX). Companies like Lumen Technologies and Fidelity Investments are adopting this approach to enhance both customer satisfaction and employee productivity, recognizing that these aspects are deeply intertwined. The strategy aims to create exponential business value by addressing experiences holistically rather than in silos, despite the current lack of a single, all-encompassing platform.

title: Amazon renews Prime credit card tie-up with JPMorgan Chase after flirting with American Express
summary: Amazon has renewed its agreement with JPMorgan Chase to issue its flagship Prime rewards credit card, following months of intense negotiations where other financial institutions like American Express and Synchrony also vied for the lucrative partnership. The deal maintains the card's rich 5% rewards rate for Amazon.com and Whole Foods purchases and highlights the significant value these co-brand credit card partnerships hold for issuing banks. This renewal continues a long-standing relationship between Amazon and JPMorgan, dating back to 2002.

title: The Unintended Consequences of Taxing Unrealized Capital Gains
summary: President Biden's proposed "Billionaire Minimum Income Tax" targets households worth over $100 million and would levy a 20% tax on both realized and unrealized capital gains. This article argues that taxing unrealized gains, such as the appreciation of a home not yet sold, could have significant negative consequences, including forcing billionaires like Elon Musk to sell large portions of their company stock, potentially impacting the broader market and 401(k)s. The author contends that the proposal is driven by envy and misunderstands the tax contributions already made by high-income earners.

title: Macy's building N.C. distribution center, 2,800 jobs to come
summary: Macy's Inc. announced plans to build a $584 million distribution and online order fulfillment center in China Grove, North Carolina. This project is expected to create about 2,800 jobs, with the facility opening in 2024 and handling 30% of Macy's digital supply chain capacity. The company could receive up to $2.3 million in state grants and additional state and local incentives valued at $58 million.

title: GameStop Soars on Plans to Extend Rebound With Stock Split
summary: GameStop (GME) shares soared by as much as 22% in extended trading following the announcement of plans to propose a stock split to shareholders in the form of a dividend. The company intends to ask for approval to increase its Class A shares from 300 million to 1 billion at its upcoming annual meeting. This move led to a significant jump in the stock price, reaching $203.98 after closing at $166.58.
